newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rangebound Australian stocks end just firmer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rangebound Australian stocks end just firmer.

text.p: AORD 2388.60 +2.30 DJIA closed
SPI futures 2385 -12 US 30yr closed
10yrbond futs 92.815 -0.040 Gold (Lon Fix) 372.20 -.80
AUD 0.8110 (Thu 0.8102) CRB Index closed
*Stocks edge just firmer by close, fail to escape nine point range in mixed trade. Volume 624.85 million shares, value A$1.63 bln, 1,091 stocks traded, 344 steady, 403 up, 344 down.
The Australian share market edged just firmer by the close on Friday with mixed performances from the leaders ensuring the market failed to escape a nine-point range established early in the day.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 2.3 points at 2,388.6. December share price index futures were 12 points lower at 2,385 and at a 3.6 point discount to the index.

With the US on Thanksgiving holiday and local October balance payments data that passed barely noticed, the market went into pre-weekend mode with options-boosted turnover figures belying a modest day's activity.

"Very much a neutral sort of day. We had no lead from the U.S. on either bonds, equities or commodities," said a Brisbane dealer, pointing to a patchy performance from the majors that saw the broader market end virtually unchanged.
"Losses in a few stocks were offset by gains in the National Australia Bank while the heavy turnover was largely options-related."
National Australia Bank shares leapt to record highs after its announced a A$1.1 billion share buyback scheme.
"National Australia Bank was the standout in the leaders," the dealer said.
Other features remained elusive as traders awaited the reopening of the U.S. markets.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to six, while about 32 percent of shares traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade saw moderate activity while options trade was slow. Total options traded 29,429 Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 5,639

In other local markets, Australian bond yields ended below the day's highs, but never looked like making a full recovery after an early sharp sell-off as events this week left the monetary policy outlook unclear.
The benchmark 10-year bond yield came close to testing 7.25 percent just after the opening, having brushed 7.0 percent at the start of the week and by 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT) was yielding 7.19 percent.
The Australian dollar wound down a week of steady consolidation in suitably composed style Friday and kept a firm grip on the 81 cent level.

The currency was working out a heavily overbought position after last week's wildly impulsive 2-1/2 cent rally and further restrained by options-related offers in the US$0.8130/50 area. By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.8106/11.
